text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
- Small and medium-sized companies have a tough time surviving in Norway. A study shows that two years ago 18,000 of small and medium-size companies 66,000 were making losses.
- Last year insurance companies paid more than 1.3 billion crowns to cover damage done by narcotics addicts to property, including burglary and car thefts.
- Torunn Anfinsen in the northern city of Tromsoe has designed a bikini made of sheep skin for bathing during the Arctic summer.

- The stock market was relieved when Norsk Hydro presented its first-quarter result, which was much better than the fourth quarter of 1996. The result beat market expectations and Hydro's share price rocketed on the Oslo Bourse.

- Norway may be forced to impose export quotas on farmed salmon to the European Union market. This could be a compromise proposal by the EU in the negotiations about possibly slapping anti-dumping duties on salmon imported from Norway.
- The market capitalisation of Norsk Hydro increased by five billion crowns yesterday after CEO Egil Myklebust presented surprisingly good first-quarter profits.

- Airlines SAS and Braathens are trying to block attempts by the Norwegian Finance Ministry to look at their lists of passengers who run up bonus points on air miles. The ministry wants to tax such bonuses.
